It closes with tiered sample syllabus language ranging from full prohibition to permitted use with citation.

documents.summary: Tier 4: A three-page student guide that defers course-level rules to each instructor's syllabus and sets cross-cutting expectations on original work, citation, copyright of course materials, privacy, and social and environmental impact. It then gives advice for when AI is allowed (verify output, ask for guidance rather than answers, document prompts) and restates KPU's rule that personal study use is not a breach if outputs are not submitted or used in exams.

documents.title: Guidance on the acceptability of using generative AI in coursework
documents.summary: Tier 4: Non-binding guidance from the Provost's AI Task Force clarifying course-outline expectations for generative AI. Instructors choose whether and how AI is used and must communicate it; silence implies use is unrestricted, while students are told to assume possible restriction. It addresses privacy impact assessment before requiring tools, alternative assignments for students unable to use AI, citation, and sample syllabus statements.

Instructors decide whether to use AI, must communicate expectations and disclose their own use, provide equitable access and opt-outs, and may not use AI detectors to substantiate misconduct; privacy and student consent rules apply. A short student section covers verification, responsibility, and transparency.
